messages:
Jordan: Running into a TS annoyance in the JS SDK sample for edge runtimes. Types break during worker bundle check.
Priya: What's the error text?
Jordan: TL;DR: overloads + generics + unknown. Example signature: `export function invoke<T>(req: {payload: T}): Promise<string>; export function invoke(req: {payload: unknown}): Promise<string>;`
Jordan: Calling `sdk.invoke({payload: {x:1}})` ends up with payload typed as unknown and TS yells `Type 'unknown' is not assignable to type 'T'`. Works fine in local Node CJS build.
Sam: Could be bundler/tsconfig differences for edge. Which tsconfig and TS version?
Jordan: sample tsconfig uses `module: ESNext`, `moduleResolution: bundler`, `target: ES2020`. GH actions uses TS 5.1.
Lee: Overload selection can be order-dependent. If the fallback with unknown sits first, inference chooses it. Swap so the generic overload is declared first. Also a `helper<T>(...)` wrapper can force inference.
Priya: We prefer keeping `unknown` in public APIs for safety. But if it breaks inference for common patterns we should either: (1) add explicit generic-first overloads, or (2) offer a user-friendly wrapper in our SDK docs.
Sam: Another consideration: published .d.ts layout and package `exports` can affect resolution. Confirm we ship d.ts aligned to ESM paths.
Jordan: Tried reorder and helper wrapper — helper works, reorder helps too. Changing fallback to `any` also works but we'd rather not.
Lee: Action items: Jordan to push minimal repro to samples and open PR with (a) helper wrapper fix and (b) sample tsconfig tuned for Cloudflare/Edge. Priya to add a short docs blurb "Why explicit generics sometimes needed". Sam to run types-check on samples via ci-bot.
ci-bot: queued types check for samples/edge-quickstart (ts=5.1, node=18)
Jordan: I'll include tests showing the inference regression and the wrapper fix. Will ping when PR lands.
Priya: Also create an audit ticket for public APIs that use `unknown` and decide per-API whether to add overloads or change to stricter generics.
Lee: Good. Also remind folks to include a copyable tsconfig in samples to reduce onboarding friction.
Jordan: Thanks all, will follow up with links.
